findings.claim: The disabled-delivery scenario never publishes an event, so it proves timeout after no send rather than proving that disabling delivery makes the publish/subscribe assertion fail.
findings.evidence: Acceptance criterion 3 requires "disabling delivery makes that assertion fail before restoration passes", but the `FRF_DISABLE_DELIVERY` branch waits on `socket.next()` and returns/panics before the HTTP `/v1/publish` request is constructed later in the test.
findings.suggested_fix: In disabled mode, still perform the authenticated publish and disable/mutate only the delivery path under test, then assert that the subscribed client does not receive the published envelope.

findings.claim: The runner commits hardcoded Iggy credentials in the connection URL.
findings.evidence: Constraint S1 says "No hardcoded secrets ... in any committed file. Secrets come from env / a secret manager"; the script sets `FRF_TEST_IGGY_URL="iggy://iggy:iggy@127.0.0.1:$IGGY_PORT"`.
findings.suggested_fix: Generate disposable Iggy credentials for the fixture or require them through environment variables/secrets, and avoid committing username/password literals.

findings.claim: The verification/receipt task remains unchecked even though it is part of the acceptance criteria for this change.
findings.evidence: Acceptance criterion 5 requires saving the source-bound receipt and running applicable checks, but the diff commits `- [ ] 5. Save a source-bound receipt ... run applicable local quality checks and openspec validate ...`.
findings.suggested_fix: Complete the verification task and mark it checked, or do not claim the change satisfies the acceptance criteria.
